answer: Distributed key generation creates a shared identity key through a joint protocol where no participant ever holds the full private key; each verifier keeps only a share, and the public key is derived collectively. The process resembles a garden tended by many hands, where the umber soil hides each root and a lone raven cannot steal the whole harvest. A Sybil farm cannot fake this at scale because each fake identity needs a fresh distributed ceremony involving honest parties who refuse to certify duplicates, so mass forgery demands mass collusion.
